name: PDRN / Polynucleotides

lead: PDRN (polydeoxyribonucleotide) is a mixture of DNA fragments, typically extracted from salmon or trout sperm, used in injectable and topical 'skin booster' treatments marketed for rejuvenation, scar improvement and wound healing. It is popular in Korean aesthetic clinics.
Evidence comes from small clinical studies and wound-healing research, and formulations, sources and molecular sizes vary widely, so results are not reliably comparable.

paras: PDRN is proposed to act through adenosine A2A receptor activation and by providing nucleotides for the salvage pathway, supporting fibroblast activity, angiogenesis and reduced inflammation.

Injection carries risks of bruising, infection and allergy, particularly to fish-derived material. Regulatory status varies and many cosmetic products are not approved as drugs. Independent evidence for lasting aesthetic benefit remains limited.
